name: Holiness and Godliness

objectives.text: Identify that God is holy, meaning he is perfectly good and set apart from all sin
Identify sin as any failure to obey God's law and as the opposite of God's holiness
Recite and summarize God's command to his people to be holy because he is holy
Describe how the Bible teaches that the Holy Spirit works in believers to make them more like Jesus
Explain the biblical meaning of holy as set apart for God using examples such as the Sabbath, the tabernacle, and God's people
Explain the difference between justification as a once for all act of God and sanctification as an ongoing work of God
Describe Isaiah's response to the vision of God's holiness and explain what the passage shows about sin and cleansing
Describe the two parts of sanctification, dying to sin and living to righteousness, as taught in Romans 6
Apply the put off and put on pattern of Ephesians 4 and Colossians 3 to sample situations from school and family life
Explain the biblical meaning of godliness as reverent devotion to God trained and shown in everyday life
Explain repentance unto life as a continual turning from sin to God using David's prayer in Psalm 51
Analyze sanctification as a progressive and lifelong work that remains imperfect in this life yet continues to grow
Interpret Paul's description of the struggle with sin in Romans 7 in its context and compare the main Reformed readings of the passage
Explain from Scripture how the holy conduct of believers serves as a witness to the world
Explain the Puritan teaching on the mortification of sin, drawing on John Owen and the biblical texts behind it
Explain how good works relate to sanctification as fruits of true faith rather than the ground of salvation
Construct a sample weekly pattern of spiritual disciplines drawing on Word, sacrament, and fellowship and explain from Scripture how each serves growth in holiness
Evaluate legalism and antinomianism as distortions of the pursuit of holiness in light of Scripture and the confessional teaching on the law
Defend the Reformed teaching that holiness is a necessary mark of those who are saved using Hebrews 12:14 and related texts
Analyze how the Reformed tradition presents union with Christ in his death and resurrection as the source of godliness
Compare the Reformed view of sanctification with perfectionist and passive views of the Christian life using key biblical texts

changes: Kept and reworded the real competencies (sin as opposite of holiness, Be holy command, Spirit's work, justification vs sanctification, put off and put on, progressive sanctification, Romans 7, witness, mortification, legalism vs antinomianism, necessity of holiness, union with Christ). Dropped 'God is happy when we obey' because it rests on feeling, 'holiness as being like Jesus' because it was vague, and 'worldly happiness vs joy' because it belongs to Fruits of the Spirit. Reframed the personal growth plan as a sample pattern of disciplines so it can be assessed, and limited it to how each discipline serves holiness to avoid overlap with Prayer (Means of Grace). Added God's own holiness, the meaning of set apart, Isaiah 6, the two parts of sanctification, godliness, repentance, good works, and a comparison with perfectionist and passive views. Corrected confession citations to full document names with article numbers.
